My first touch froze my mother to gold.
I was born with golden eyes.
When she held me for the first time, 
her skin hardened beneath my fingers.
At five, I grabbed a pack boy during a game
He froze mid-laugh.
At eight, I touched a beggar’s last bread.
It became pure gold in my hands.
The pack called me cursed
But my father called me opportunity.
He bartered me 
for ten million dollars.
That was the beginning of my doom. 
Alpha Edward didn’t see a child. He saw a mine. "
He burned my palms with hot iron rods,
trying to force gold from my skin.
Something white sparks before he could break me.
And the Moon Goddess descended,
“I am taking the child’s blessing, when she turns eighteen, she will take everything from you.”
A golden light tore from my hands 
and vanished into the sky.
My power disappeared. But my suffering didn’t.
Alpha Edward grew afraid.
So he handed me to his daughter.
“Make her your slave. Suppress her before she outshines you.”
Marcy obeyed. She didn’t kill me. She ended me slowly.
Years of hunger.
Bruises.
Chains.
Servitude. "
Today, I cook for two hundred wolves without sleep everyday.
I am 18 now but nothing changed."I want to give up", I whispered to the moon goddess in pain.
I was answered. And everything was about to change in a blink.
Merge-
There were whispers through the pack. Electric, hushed, breathless. A visitor was coming.
Alpha Damon.

Leader of the Dark Howlers, fiercest pack in the realm. He was the most powerful Alpha in all of North America. Women threw themselves at him. Rulers feared him. He could seduce a she-wolf with a glance, or tear out a man’s throat just as easily.
Damon was untouchable. 
He scorned the idea of love. Rejected every political match. Not a single potential bride, despite the many presented, could win his affection. None were worthy of being his Luna, the proud she-wolf to rule by his side.
Love was a distraction, an attempt to tame him. And Damon would never be tamed. 
Still, there were those who tried. 

Alpha Edward, leader of the Red Moon pack, was desperate to secure his political power. He invited Damon to meet his daughter, Princess Marcy, beautiful, cunning, cruel. She intended to make him hers.
Talia feared their union. Would Marcy succeed where so many others had failed? Would Marcy’s cruelty only intensify as Luna to such a powerful Alpha? 

The moment Alpha Damon stepped onto Red Moon Pack grounds with his mated Betas, Caden and Maya, something felt off. His wolf stirred uneasily beneath the surface. Damon didn’t need confirmation, he already knew: no one in the Red Moon Pack could be trusted.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”

While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.

When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?

Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'

Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled.  In confirmation, I couldnt my wolf had been silenced years ago. 

My name is Talia, but no one calls me Talia except for teachers on the first day of schooling. I'm more popular as the wolfless freak. I'm a werewolf in the red moon pack. Since I'm an orphan, I'm not completely sure how old I am, but I'm pretty sure I'm 16. Also, I'm an omega, which means I'm a servant. My job is to make the meals for the werewolves who live in the pack house. Between making breakfast and dinner for over 100 wolves, cleaning up after them, and restocking the pantries of the ranked members' apartments on the 3rd and 4th floors, I do normal teenager stuff, except I don't have a lot of spare time to do so. Homework is the extent of living my teen life. Right now it's 11:30 at night. I'm putting the finishing touches on my English essay when I hear the door of the dungeon slam open. Great. Now what did I do? It doesn't take much. 
Alpha Edward is an alcoholic. It's really difficult for werewolves to get drunk, which means you have to drink heavily to feel the effects. This means he probably had a fight with Luna Layla about his drinking. Which means she locked him out of their room. Which means he has come down to take out his anger on me. Just an average Tuesday in the packhouse. I know the drill. I'm already on my feet waiting for him. I'm thinking in my mind. “Alpha Edward, what can I do for you?" I ask with my eyes looking at the floor. I keep my hands clasped in front of me, trying to look as small as possible. Without a word, a whiskey bottle whizzes past my ear and smashes against the wall above my cot. I flinch and can't help but start to tremble and hug myself. Whatever is about to happen it's going to be worse than usual. He lunges forward and grabs me by the throat with both hands. I feel tears coming to my eyes as the lack of oxygen turns the edges of my vision dark. I desperately claw at his hands, trying to escape his grip but it's no use. He picks me up by the neck so I'm at face level with him. His eyes are pitch indicating his wolf Ruckus is at the surface. His breath stinks because of alcohol. I start gagging and choking from the lack of oxygen. Without warning, he throws me across the room as if I weigh nothing. My back slams against the wall and I land on my back on the cot. The shards of the broken bottle pierce the skin on my back through my thin t-shirt. The whiskey makes the cuts burn. I try to muffle a scream as the pain sears through me. He comes across the room and picks me up roughly by the hair. I feel the shards of glass cutting deeper as he pulls me up. He throws me to the ground. The glass bits are grinding deeper into my back. I can feel something wet soaking through my shredded shirt. I don't dare move and make him even madder. I feel my ribs snap when his foot makes contact. One of his feet lands on my jaw. I feel a sickening snap. Rattle in my brain. The metallic taste instantly fills my mouth. Alpha Edward has been using me as his punching bag for years, but this was way more intense than it has ever been before. In the past couple of years, he started dipping the whip in wolfsbane, which makes me heal slower, so now I have gnarly scars across my back and arms. I managed to eke out. My voice is small and garbled. He abruptly stops and walks out of the room. He comes back a moment later with the whip and starts lashing my back relentlessly. The whip is dripping with wolfsbane. The lashes, combined with the glass shards still in my back, combined with the wolfbane are too much. My vision turns blurry and I pass out. Numbness surrounds me. Is this what being dead is like? It's peaceful, but a little bit boring. At least I don't have to feed the pack. Oh dang, I didn't get a chance to turn in that English essay. It was a good one too. The constant soft beeps are soothing. I don't know how long I've been dead, but I feel like I want to open my eyes, ready to take on the afterlife. After what seems like forever, I'm able to open my eyes and find I'm alone in soft comfort in a brightly lit, clean room. This is the afterlife? Maybe this is some sort of waiting area, but where's the lobby? Is there a receptionist? My mind slowly becomes more clear and I realize I'm not dead.I'm in the pack hospital. I need to leave before the Alpha finds me outside the dungeon. I try to get up but I can barely move my body. Every move causes excruciating pain. I start to panic, making the beeps in the room become faster. Oh, I'm hooked up to a bunch of machines. I try to figure out how to unhook them so no one hears the noises. Too late, I hear people in the hallway getting closer. I try to sit up. I need to ignore the pain. I have to escape. I slowly slide off the side of the legs. My legs were wobbly. The tubes and wires sticking out of me prevent me from getting too far. The door opens and the pack doctor comes in with a nurse. The doctor is an older person. “Ah, Talia. You're awake. Let's get you back on the mat, shall we?" The doctor says gently. He and the nurse come to either side of me and reach out to hold my arms. A deep growl escapes my chest. “Don't touch me," I snap, shaking them off. My voice is scratchy and raw and my mouth feels like a thousand needles are poking into it. “It's alright, Talia. No one is going to hurt you here. We're trying to help you heal. Let's get you back to and get you a drink of water," the doctor raises his hands in surrender. I look at him hesitantly before accepting their help. The nurse hands me a cup of water with a straw. The water feels good on my throat. The doctor sits in the chair beside the bed as the nurse checks my vitals and starts messing with the tubes and wires attached to me. “Talia, you had surgery to remove hundreds of shards of glass from your back, we also had to reset some ribs, your jaw, and you had a lot of wolfsbane in your blood. We gave you a transfusion to clear it from your system so you could heal," the doctor explains, "You're lucky your wound isn’t badly serious.” Sure about that last part, doctor? I think to myself. “When the pack realized breakfast had not been prepared, Tony went to get you and found you on the ground in your...uh...room," he looked at me with sympathy, "Talia, who did this to you? It's a crime that could be grounds for banishment from the pack. Based on the scarring, this isn't the first time you've been attacked.” I can't answer him. I stare at my hands on my lap quietly. How can I tell him Alpha Edward is the one who caused this? There's no way he'd believe me, even if he did, what are they going to do? Banish the Alpha? Fat chance of that. I decide my best move is to just shake my head no. I don't want to get out of the pack for lying. I have nowhere to go. I would be nothing. “Okay. Let's move on to the next question. When do you turn seventeen?" He looks at the papers inside his folder. “I-I don't know exactly, sir," I say honestly. He looks at me with a furrowed brow. He glances at the nurse and asks her to give us privacy for a few minutes. Am I in trouble? I just woke up, I don't know what I could have done. She finishes what she's doing and leaves the room. “You don't know your birthday, Talia?" he asks, confused. “M-my father brought me here when I was a baby. He was a bad guy. Alpha Edward, well...he..." I feel my face burning with embarrassment. My hands tremble and tears threaten to escape my eyes. I didn't think I would have to tell this story to the doctor. I thought everyone already knew. My father was a bad guy. Alpha Edward ended his life for coming into pack territory without permission. They didn't realize he was carrying a baby until they unzipped his jacket and saw I was tucked inside. It was a miracle I survived. Since I was just a baby, they couldn't just get rid of me but they didn't know anything about me. I was wrapped in a blanket that had the name 'Talia’' embroidered on it. So, that is what they called me. My father could have been a kidnapper for all I know. The only reason they gave me the last name Jackman is because after they took down my father, they looked through his wallet to identify him. The only form of ID he had was a library card that said Brian Jackman on it. I've tried an internet search for his name on the computer in the school library before. Nothing comes up in the search. “You don't need to finish, I know what happened to your father.” “Well, after that...happened...Luna Layla took me in until I was old enough to start school. Then she moved me into the dungeon. I've kinda been on my own since then. I never found out when my actual birthday was. To be honest, you're the first person who has ever asked. I mean, I guess I'm sixteen. My wolf hasn't woken up yet.” The doctor nods, looking at me with pity. Almost like he cares. He asks me a few more questions about my medical history, but there's nothing to speak of. I don't remember ever being treated by a doctor before. “I see," he closes the folder and tucks his pen into his shirt pocket, "Well, I know you haven't had a chance to look in the mirror yet, but when you do, you may find you look a little different. Don't be alarmed. I've done as many tests as I could think of. It is not medically related.” I look at him with confusion, "Y-yes, sir." I assume he means I'm healing faster but, why did he need me to look in the mirror? Why not just tell me? I look at the nurse who is staring at me. When she realizes I caught her, her eyes dart away. What's that about? Okay, lady. Rude. “I'll leave you now," she says, "You can go in the bathroom and wash up. Just take that pole with the IV solution with you. There are lounge shorts and fresh underwear in the bag. You need to leave the hospital gown on until your back heals. Alright?” “Yes, ma'am. Thank you, Diane," she nods and leaves the room. It's the first time in my life people have been kind to me. I mean, I think it's part of their job but still. All I have known so far were insults, physical misery, and hard work. Never any kindness, never any. I feel like I can trust the doctor but I'm still wary of Nurse Diane. The way she stared at me just now makes me uncomfortable. I pick up the duffle bag and go to the bathroom. I avoid looking in the mirror. Everything in the bathroom is fresh. There's a shower, but I'm worried the pressure of the water will hurt my back. I decided to fill the tub halfway and get in. The water is warm and soothing. There's a washcloth and a fresh bar of soap. I clean myself until the water is gross. I drain the tub, wipe out the ring of dirt around the edge, and fill it again. The water is not nearly as dirty as this time when I finish washing. I find it hard to raise my hands, but I don't want to call the nurse to help me. I gently wash my hair, dry off and wrap the soft towel around my head. There's a toothbrush and a small tube of paste on the shelf by the sink. I'm living in the lap of luxury in the pack hospital! I pick them up and start brushing my teeth. I can't avoid it anymore, I need to look in the mirror. I finally worked up the courage to take a peek. What I see makes me drop the toothbrush. My face is still covered in bruises, but that's not what made me drop the toothbrush. The iris of my left eye is violet. Not like a shade of blue that could be a little purple in the right light. No. My right pupil is still the drab gray I'm used to but my left pupil looks crazy. I blink my eyes hard a few times. Still the same. I tried rubbing my eye but it doesn't make a difference. There's no mistaking it - my eye is bright, practically glowing...violet. The two days seem to last forever. I'm not complaining though. I've never gotten so much in my life and as a bonus, I get three meals a day. Three! I keep looking in the mirror. I can't get over how weird my purple eye looks. I wake up on the second day and go to the bathroom to freshen up. I stare at myself in the mirror for the millionth time. My left eye is still violet. Now my right eye seems like it's starting to turn violet as well. There was nothing I could do about it, so I decided to try not to worry. Since Red Moon is a pretty big pack, we have a high school on pack territory. The library has a really big werewolf lore research section. I will do some research during lunch. As I tilt my head to the side to brush my hair, I notice a chunk of my hair has changed color. Instead of my normal mousy brown, it is silvery gray. Okay seriously now. What is going on? What is happening to me? Is this a trick? Is there bleach in the shampoo or something? If it is a trick, it isn't funny. I pick up the bottle and smell it. It smells like strawberries, not bleach. Weird. I have never heard of a wolf's eye or hair color changing when they are coming of age but that's what the doctor thinks is happening. Diane comes in just after lunch with paperwork and pamphlets for me. She hands me another little bag, "Just a little something to help you stay incognito until you are finished healing," she says. "Thank you for everything," I say as I open the bag. There is a baseball cap and a pair of dark sunglasses. "How do I look?" I ask as I model them for her. She giggles at my poses, "You're a star, darling." Maybe she isn't so bad after all. She gives me a gentle hug and sends me on my way. I have another two hours before I need to start prepping dinner. I decided to take my new clothes to my room and clean up the mess down there so I can tonight. Something smells different as I walk down the hall of the dungeon, like a cleaning solution. I turn on my lamp to find the room has been transformed. My lamp is not sitting on an old stack of milk crates. It is on a nightstand. There is a new one too, my old cot is gone. I have a proper. Complete with new sheets and blankets. There is also a small desk and chair with all my school books arranged in a basket next to it. I must be dreaming. That or I walked into someone else's room by accident, except no one else lives down here. You can barely tell it was an old dungeon cell. It looks like what I imagine a dorm room would look like. I peek out of the doorway to make sure I am in the right place. I seem to be. What gives? I walk over and sit carefully as if it will disappear if I move too fast. It is like a cloud. The gray and turquoise linens are fresh and new. There are even two pillows. I never had a proper pillow before, let alone two. As far as I know, Diane is the only one who came down here while I was in the hospital. Could she have had all this done? Surely she will get in trouble when Alpha Edward finds out. Then I remember she doesn't know how much the Alpha hates me. I don't know how I'm going to explain it when he finds out but I won't tattle on anyone for trying to help me either. I put my new clothes away in the drawers of the nightstand. I stash the duffle bag under the mattress. Once I am seventeen, I will figure out a way to get out of this place. Find a new pack that will accept a violet-eyed weakling of a wolf. I sit at the desk and write a thank you letter to the doctor and Nurse Diane. I turn in the chair looking around the like-new room. I am in awe that someone would do this for me. I must have been daydreaming because I don't hear the door at the top of the stairs, but I hear two sets of footsteps coming down the hall. Instantly I freeze. I can smell Alpha Edward's scent getting closer. I don't know who the other scent belongs to. Instinctively, I scramble and stand in the middle of the room just as they get to the doorway. He leans against the frame and crosses his arms in front of himself. I can feel my whole trembling as he stares. My eyes are glued to the ground. I do not want him to see my new eye color shining through. "C-can I help y-you, Alpha Edward?" "That little stunt you pulled cost me a lot of money," he says with a calm, gravelly voice, "And when you cost me money, you cost my whole family money." "I'm sorry, sir," I apologize, although I have no idea what stunt he is talking about. I look up just enough to see Marcy, the Alpha's daughter, is also standing in the doorway. Marcy takes a step closer and I can feel tears starting to sting the corners of my eyes as my arms shake uncontrollably. How am I going to face her at school? I haven't had a conversation with her since her mom made me live in the dungeon, anyway. But as far as I know, she had no idea I live down here now. She is going to tell everyone for sure. "Surgery and hospital stays aren't cheap, Talia," Alpha Edward sneers from the doorway, "And do you know how disgusting the food has been for the past two and a half days?" I just nod, still looking at the ground. I'm not trying to argue with a lunatic. It isn't my fault I had to have surgery. He's the one who broke a bottle and threw me into the broken pieces! If he hadn't, I would have been just fine. I would have been able to bounce back the next day and make breakfast like I was supposed to, even if I was banged up. There is a pause and he finally growls, "Where did all this furniture come from? Did you steal it?” “N-no, sir. I-I...it was here when I g-got back from the hospital wing. I don't know wh-who brought it.” "You owe me, Talia. You also owe whoever turned your room into this comfortable space. You'll work in the packhouse until you pay it back every cent. For the rest of your life if necessary. No more school. You don't need education to cook and clean." He uses his Alpha tone. I cannot disobey. With those words, the small flame of hope in my heart extinguishes. I don't get paid so I don't know how I could ever pay back any debt. Luna Layla told me years ago that the room in the dungeon was payment enough for my services. I am less than an omega now. I am a slave. "Marcy, teach her a lesson for wasting our money." "Yes, Alpha.” Tears stream down my face as the reality of my fate sets in. Alpha Edward is passing the torch of his cruelty down to his daughter. But I know better than that. He will never stop. Marcy reaches forward and claps the back of my neck. She forces me down into a bowing position and growls deeply, "You should be grateful my father doesn't banish you. If you were a rogue, I would make sure you never made it to the border of the territory." A squeak escapes my throat. I am so scared I feel like I am going to pass out. Marcy turns to her father, "Don't worry, Alpha. I've got this situation covered." I hear Alpha Edward's footsteps walk back down the hallway as he leaves the dungeon. Marcy tightens her grip on my neck, extending her wolf claws, making me yelp. As soon as the door slams, Marcy releases my neck and kneels in front of me. Her face is contorted with anger. She grabs my shoulders, shaking me roughly, "What did you do to make him so mad?" Why isn't she doing anything to me like she told Alpha Edward she would? I stiffened my whole body, avoiding eye contact with her. I'm shaking, I can't even speak now. The thought of two people doing something bad to me regularly for the rest of my life...it just can't be real. Can it? How can the Moon Goddess allow this to happen? I want to leave the world. That's not an exaggeration. That's not me being dramatic. Please, Moon Goddess, don't let this happen. Just let me go. I shake so badly that I fall to my knees. I start to sob hysterically and my brain shuts down from being able to think rationally. Marcy grabs my chin and forces me to look at her in her cold gray eyes. She looks at me in horror for a moment, "What happened to your eyes?” She moves her hands up from my chin to just below my eyes. It feels like her hands are trembling against my face. "A-are you a mixed-blood or something?" All I can manage is to shake my head no between sobs. As I shake my head, I feel her starting to press her thumbs against my lower eyelids obstructing my vision. Oh no, she’s going to poke my eyes out. She saw the violet color. She was going to blind me. I place my hands on top of her trying to push her away. I hear myself screaming, "NO! STOP!! Don't take my eyes out! PLEASE!!!” For just a moment, time freezes. I don't mean like it feels like time is standing still because I'm in the middle of a traumatic situation. No, time is frozen. Well, frozen for everything except for me I should say. I can feel it in the air. It only lasts for a moment. I pulled Marcy's hands away from my face easily. The look of anger combined with confusion is stuck on her face. Next to her, a fly is suspended in mid-air. The second hand on the clock has stopped on the wall behind her. Drips of water aren't finished falling, leaving umbrella-shaped splashes in the puddles on the floor. What? Did the Moon Goddess hear me? Did she have mercy on me? Did she let my dream come true? I look back at Marcy with wide eyes. My hands are glowing purple. As quickly as it stopped, time started again. Marcy starts screaming and pushes herself away from me. The tops of her hands where my hands were touching her were burnt. I look down at my hands. They are normal again, not glowing purple. Seriously though, what happened? I shut my eyes tight, waiting for Marcy to retaliate. “If you tell anyone, I will kill you," she says in my ear. Then she punches me in the stomach, knocking the air out of my lungs. I hear her footsteps running down the hall, then out the door. I don't know how long I sit like this but when I finally open my eyes I breathe a sigh of relief. I lean against my body for a while longer, sobbing, shaking, and trying to catch my breath. She didn't harm me? Surely she was coming back. I sniff the air but her scent is gone. I listened carefully but there were no sounds in other parts of the dungeon. I'm alone. “Moon Goddess, thank you for saving me. Thank you," I say out loud, just in case the miracle I just experienced was because of her. I feel exhausted, but starting to feel calmer. Okay Talia, focus. I need to make dinner for the pack or Alpha Edward will find me and kill me. I don't think it's an exaggeration, either. Even if I try to run away, either he or Marcy would find me before I could get off the territory. I take a few deep breaths and make myself go down the hall to wash up at the sink. I splash cold water on my face and look in the grungy mirror. Both of my eyes are pure violet now. The silver streaks are starting to take over my hair now. It isn't like an old person's hair. It is silvery that almost shimmers, even in the low light of the dungeon. So weird, there's no way I'm going to be able to get used to this new look. I go back to my room and get dressed in leggings and a T-shirt. I put on the baseball cap Diane gave me, pulling the brim low to hide my eyes. Throughout dinner, I receive murderous glares from Alpha Edward. I make sure to keep my eyes to the floor so Alpha Edward would avoid seeing the color. Marcy glares at me every chance she gets. After dinner, it takes longer than usual to stock pantries because whoever did it while I was in the hospital had no idea what they were doing. It is well after midnight when I flop down on my and close my eyes. June 20th, I think to myself. It's the last day of school. Well, for other people anyway, not me. You don't need the education to cook and stock pantries, Alpha Edward's words ring in my ears. Just another day for me, I suppose. I wallow in self-pity for a bit before I roll over and try to fall asleep. I'm almost asleep when I hear a woman's voice. "Hello!" I quickly scramble to my feet, looking everywhere for who it could be. I'm the only one in the room. I peek into the hallway and look around but no one is there either. "Hello?" I whisper loudly down the hallway. "Ugh, Talia. This is no way for a warrior to behave. Get yourself together," the voice chides. I realize the voice is coming from inside my head. "Who.. who are you?" I ask hesitantly, worried that I've gone insane. "I am the messenger of the Moon Goddess. The whisperer of the moon. But I like you, so I’ll let you call me Sylvie." Alice gestured down the hall.
“Come on. Before this gets worse.”
As she knocked Principal Jameson's office, a voice called out, "Come in."

She smiled as Violet walked in. "Welcome, Violet."  But her smile faltered when she saw the bruise marks on Violet's neck.
"Who did this to you?" she demanded, her voice full of worry.
For the first time since arriving, Violet felt a flicker of hope. Finally, someone was going to deal with that jerk. She quickly explained what had happened, describing the red haired guy in detail. But as she spoke, Principal Jameson's expression changed from anger to something much worse: fear.
"You mean Griffin Hale did this to you?"
"Griffin Hale? Is that his name?" Violet asked. 
"Yes, Miss Purple," Principal Jameson began, her voice suddenly cautious. “And you shouldn’t be cavorting with him on your first day.”
She exhaled slowly, fingers tightening on the edge of her desk.
“There are… expectations here, Miss Purple.”
Violet frowned. “About what?”
Jameson hesitated.
“About who gets noticed. Who gets protected.”
Violet crossed her arms. “And who doesn’t.”
Jameson didn’t argue.
“Most of that attention is already spoken for,” she said carefully. “Bloodlines. Families. Girls who were raised for this world.”
Violet looked up.
“There is one student in particular,” Jameson added. “A very special one…”
Violet's stomach tightened. "You're talking about Autumn Carson."
Jameson looked up, surprised. "You've heard the name."
"Hard not to. Everyone here says it like a prayer."
Jameson's voice lowered. "Then you understand what you're walking into."
"What I don't understand is why it involves me."
Jameson exhaled slowly.
"Because something reacted to you."
"Something?"
"One of them," she corrected. "Possibly more than one."
“And I’m guessing that’s not possible.”
Jameson’s expression darkened.
“It shouldn’t be.”
Silence stretched between them.
“If you are compatible with one of the Cardinal Alphas,” Jameson said carefully, “it changes things.”
“For who?”
“For everyone.”
Violet swallowed.
“And if I’m not?”
Jameson’s eyes flicked briefly toward the window… toward the Academy beyond.
“Then today was a very dangerous coincidence.”
A knock at the door.
Alice poked her head in
“Alice, take Mrs. Purple to the Infirmary,” Jameson said quietly. “Get those marks treated.”
Violet turned to leave.
“Miss Purple.”
She paused.
“If the Luna Board moves again…”
Jameson’s voice dropped.
“Pray it’s only one of them.”
Violet swallowed hard and left with Alice for the infirmary.

As they walked through the gothic Lunaris corridors, Alice reached into her bag and handed Violet a box.
“That’s your Lunaris welcome pack. Go ahead. Open it.”
Violet hesitated, then unzipped the bag. Textbooks. Supplies. And a sealed phone box.
Her breath caught.
“No way,” Violet whispered, lifting it out.
Alice smiled, all warmth again. “We give devices to scholarship students. Helps you stay connected. Just log into the Lunaris Academy app. Campus Wi-Fi is everywhere.”
Violet turned the box over in her hands.
“Come on,” Alice said brightly, already moving again. “Let’s get you to the infirmary and have those wounds checked.”
As Violet followed, phone still in her hand, the words of Principal Jameson wouldn’t leave her: “If the Luna Board moves again… Pray it’s only one of them.”
Moments later, they entered the grand, impressive infirmary ward.
A healer, one of those super-rare werewolves who could do healing magic, was lecturing a student… a guy whose arms were covered in fresh burns. 
Violet barely registered the actual healer before her attention snapped to the guy.
“You can't keep doing this to yourself, Alaric,” the healer scolded.
"I'm fine," he grumbled, obviously annoyed, as the healer's magic soothed his burns. 
Violet couldn’t be sure, but she thought she saw faint sparks crackle across his skin, dancing like trapped lightning.
And she noticed that no one else stood close enough to touch him.
He must have felt Violet staring because he turned, and their eyes met.
Holy moly. Violet forgot to breathe. Her cheeks turned pink.
He had whitish-blond hair framing a face that was ridiculously good-looking. 
But it was his eyes that really got her:
Stormy blue, like a gathering storm. 
“That’s Alpha Alaric,” Alice whispered. 
Great. Another Alpha. But this one seemed different somehow…
“No one can touch him,” Alice added.
“Why?” Violet asked.

Alice didn’t answer, but cryptically stared at the burn marks on his arms.
Violet studied him.
He had a quiet intensity, but instead of being cocky, there was an innocence about him that was strangely attractive.
With those striking sapphire eyes, he could have easily been the most handsome alpha she'd met today…
His gaze swept over her, head to toe, like he was checking her out, sending a surprising jolt through her. 
But just as quickly as that little flicker of excitement appeared, it was squashed by his  sudden cold, dismissive attitude. 
His expression made it clear: he wasn't interested. 
Any idea that he might have been was shattered by his icy indifference.
"You're good to go," the healer said, finishing up with him.
Done, Alaric brushed past Violet…
And in that quick, fleeting touch, a spark jolted through her.
It was like static shock, sharp, unexpected, and strangely exciting. 
Violet froze, her breath catching in her throat…
Alaric stopped short.
He looked down at his hand.
Then at Violet.
Confusion flickered across his face… sharp, startled, unmistakable. 
He touched her… and she was fine.
As if his lightning didn’t surge…  but recoiled.
Like it had hit something it couldn’t burn through.
His storm didn’t harm Violet. It hesitated.
How? 
For a split second, the storm in his eyes surged.
Then his expression slammed shut, colder than before.
Without a word, he turned and walked out.
Violet stood there, heart racing, skin still tingling.
“Did you see that?” Violet whispered.
Alice was staring at Alaric’s retreating back.
“That’s impossible,” Alice said under her breath.
“What is?” Violet demanded. “What just happened?”
Alice looked at her slowly.
“Alaric doesn’t touch people.”
“I noticed.”
“No,” Alice said, shaking her head. “You don’t understand. He can’t.”
Violet frowned.
“Alaric controls lightning. Not metaphorical lightning. Actual voltage. His body discharges constantly. Static. Current. Storm build-up. That’s why no one stands near him.”
Violet looked down at her own hands.
“But he touched me.”
Alice nodded once.
“And you didn’t burn.”
Violet swallowed.
Silence settled between them.
“Why?” Violet asked.
Alice hesitated.
“The Cardinal Alphas aren’t like other wolves,” she said carefully. “They were born under a lunar anomaly. People say the Moon Goddess gave them powers.”
She ticked them off quickly.
“Griffin has shockwave strength. He can level stone with a punch.”
“Roman is a Shapeshifter. Any animal. Total chaos.”
“Asher?” She lowered her voice. “Mind manipulation. Thoughts. Memories. Control.”
“And Alaric…” She glanced toward the door. “Storms. Lightning. Energy strong enough to paralyze a room.”
Violet’s skin tingled again.
“So what does it mean that I’m, like, okay?”
Alice held her gaze.
“It means one of two things. Either you’re resistant to Alpha power… or you’re compatible with it.”
The word hung between them.
Compatible.
Violet’s throat went dry.
“With him?” she asked quietly.
Alice didn’t answer right away.
“That’s the question,” she said.
Violet wondered what it all meant.
"You,” the healer interrupted. “What can I do for you?" the healer asked, her eyebrows furrowing as she looked Violet over. "You're new here, aren't you?"
Violet nodded.
"And already in the infirmary on your first day?" The healer shook her head, clucking her tongue. 
"Good luck, kid."
"I know," Violet whispered, her voice barely there. "I know."
“It's nothing serious. You're good to go,” the healer said, handing her some painkillers, and then Alice took Violet to the dorm rooms.

“Welcome to West House, Violet. This is your home now, and over there are the other houses: East, South, and North.”
“Whoa!” Violet breathed, staring at the impressive buildings.
“Ms. Purple, you see, this school is all about hierarchy. Human or werewolf, everyone forms packs in their houses. The four strongest cardinal alphas study here and run these four houses. Everyone else follows their lead. They are basically gods here.”
Violet sighed. She had already seen the glimpses of student power on her very first day.
Alice continued, “The West House you are going to be in is run by Alpha Asher Nightshade.”
Violet's stomach clenched.
Of course it was.
Of all four houses, she'd been placed in his.
The Alpha who'd humiliated her on stage. The one who'd grinned at her in the hallway like he owned her. The one who called her "purple flower" like it was already decided.
This wasn't random. It couldn't be.
“Don't worry,” Alice interrupted before Violet could ask. “Anything else? Everything you need to know is on your phone, plus your roommates will fill you in. Go meet your roommates.”

As Violet entered her room, her roommates looked at her with surprising eyes.
"No way, it's really her," one of them said, sounding shocked.
Violet raised an eyebrow. Why did everyone at this school seem to know who she was?
"Hi, I'm Lily Fairchild," a girl chirped. "It's so nice to meet you, Violet Purple!"
Violet blinked, totally surprised by the sudden friendliness.
"The grumpy one over there is Hazel Sterling," Alice said, pointing to another blonde who looked permanently scowling. 
When their eyes met, Violet immediately felt the dislike radiating from Hazel.  
Alice leaned in closer to Violet. "Hazel's just jealous of you."
Violet frowned. "What do you mean she's jealous of me?" she asked Alice, then turned to Hazel. "No offense, but we literally just met. Why would you be jealous of me? That makes zero sense."
“Offense taken!” Hazel said.
“Oh, really, Hazel? Seriously? Your ego is out of control, especially after you were just gossiping about that video,” Lily finally chimed in.
“What video?” Violet asked
All three girls turned to her, looking at her like she was totally clueless.
“You haven't checked your newsfeed,” Lily said.
"Newsfeed?" Violet echoed, even more confused.
“BioDome,” Lily explained. “It's where everyone at Lunaris Academy gets all the school news. And yeah, you're kinda trending right now.”
Before she could even grab her phone to search for this BioDome thing, Alice had hers out.
Alice searched for the video using Violet's name, and there it was.
Violet's eyes widened as the video started playing. 
It was a clip of Griffin manhandling her.
“Oh, God! Who the hell got...”
As she watched herself, awkward and vulnerable, the thought that the entire school had seen her like that burned in her chest.
“Gods, you’re so lucky,” Hazel sneered from her bed.
“Lucky?!” Violet shook her head, exasperated. ""What are you talking about? What's so special about these guys that everyone's losing their minds?"
"The Terror Four," Lily answered with a wry smile. “Most of us would kill to even be seen by them! But unfortunately, only those ranked between first and twentieth have their attention."
Violet’s stomach tightened.
She thought about the green-haired thief.
The red-haired brute.
The one with lightning under his skin.
And Asher…. The obsessive one.
This wasn’t coincidence. This felt like gravity. Forced proximity.
As if her life hadn’t started today by accident, but on schedule.
As if she hadn’t come to Lunaris to learn about the Cardinal Alphas…
But to change them.
“So,” Alice grinned. “Any Alpha you like?”
“What?” Violet blinked.
“You’re in the top twenty now,” Lily said. “They’ll see you as an equal.”
But Hazel scoffed. “Please. They’re all practically taken.”
“Yeah, but no one’s officially Luna yet,” Alice shot back.
Hazel’s smile turned sharp. “Don’t kid yourself. Autumn’s already been raised for that crown.”
Violet stiffened. “Autumn.”
For a split second, her mind traced back to Principal Jameson’s office…
“There is one student in particular,” Jameson had said. “Her name is Autumn.”
Hazel continued. “Number one. Never challenged. And she doesn’t lose.”
Autumn was the girl Lunaris had been preparing for.
The one everyone assumed would be chosen.
The one the rules were built around.
What none of them knew yet…
Was that Violet, the strange purple-haired girl standing in front of them, wasn’t meant to follow that rule. 
She was meant to break it.
For now, Violet's patience finally snapped. "All right, enough! It’s not like I am even interested." She looked each of them in the eye. "I'm so sick of the ridiculous drama at this school!"
Violet's roommates were speechless. A heavy silence filled the room.
Violet didn't wait for any response. Turning her back to them, she lay down on her bed and closed her eyes, shutting them out. Sleep came quickly, her body exhausted and her mind still buzzing from the day's craziness.
That night, Violet’s life changed!
Violet stirred in her sleep. Strong arms wrapped around her. A face buried into her purple hair.
It felt so good she instinctively snuggled closer. His scent was intoxicating. And somehow familiar…
Then she opened her eyes.
She was back on the stage of the audition. No other girls. No audience. No cameras.
Just her. And Asher.
No. This had to be a dream. He was in her head.
Alice's warning crashed through her mind: He can plant thoughts, erase memories — basically puppet-master you.
This was his power. And she was trapped inside it.
She broke free from his hold and stumbled back.
"Is this my dream?"
"I might be in your head, but this feels pretty real to me." His voice dropped to a low whisper. "And it could be real for you, too. If you let me."
Something in Violet's blood reacted… humming, answering him before her mind could stop it.
"Where's my body?" she snapped.
"Your body's in your room. Your mind's here with me."
The scene shimmered. Shifted.
When Violet blinked, she was straddling Asher on a bed in a room she'd never seen before.
Black stone walls. Candlelight. The air thick with incense.
His world. His rules.
She tried to move, but she couldn’t.
"Calm down, baby," he murmured.
Violet's skin crawled. She was disgusted by him. But her body wouldn't cooperate.
That pull was back. Stronger. Insistent.
As if her blood recognized him… even as her mind rebelled.
He looked at her with that dark, hungry gaze. Like he wanted to swallow her whole. Like he'd been waiting for her forever.
"Be mine, my purple flower," he said. "Be my queen. Rule with me."
"Let me go!" she spat.
"You're the only one who can talk to me like that and get away with it," Asher said. "Do you know how rare that is?"
"If you want to kill me, just do it. I'm not begging."
"Why would I kill my queen?"
Why was he so obsessed with her? What was it about her that he couldn't resist?
It was the same question she'd had on that stage. The same look in his eyes when she'd refused his Command. Like she was something impossible. Something he had to have.
"I'm done here," Violet snarled. "Send me back. Now."
"Sure thing," Asher replied smoothly. "But first, I need a little something to remember you by."
Scissors—then, a soft snip echoed in the silence.
A lock of her purple hair rested in his palm.
"You!" Violet exploded.
And just like at the audition — when his Command had tried to break her and failed — something inside Violet surged.
Not anger. Not fear.
Power.
The dream cracked. The candlelight flickered wild. Asher's grin faltered for the first time.
"What are you—"
She didn't let him finish. She tore herself out of his world like ripping through a wall.

Violet woke with a gasp.
Sweat soaked her sheets. Her heart was racing like she’d been running for her life.
For a second, she thought it had all been a dream.
Asher.
His hands. His voice in her head.
She stumbled into the bathroom, gripping the sink, staring at her reflection.
Her clothes were untouched. Her body unharmed.
Relief hit her…
Then her hand went to her hair.
A chunk was missing.
Violet froze.
Her fingers traced the jagged edge where purple strands should have been. 
Her stomach dropped.
It wasn’t a dream.
Asher Nightshade had been inside her head.
And he’d taken something with him.
“I need to get out of this place,” she whispered.
That thought hardened instantly.
Lunaris Academy was a trap. 
And she decided right then and there…
She wasn’t going to stay long enough to find out what else it could take from her.

Morning came too fast.
Alice burst into the room like nothing had happened, all cheer and chatter, while Violet dressed in silence.
The Lunaris Academy uniform fit perfectly. Too perfectly. Like it had been made for her.
Alice noticed the tension immediately.
The way Violet’s shoulders stayed tight. The way her eyes never quite settled, always alert.
Her smile softened.
Alice stepped closer, fixing Violet’s tie for her, hands steady… deliberate.
Protective.
“Listen, Violet,” Alice said quietly. “Power is the only currency here. If you want to be left alone, you need it.”
Violet didn’t answer.
She didn’t want power. She wanted out.
Alice held her gaze a moment longer than necessary.
As if making a silent promise.
Because Alice knew something Violet didn’t yet… She knew the secret.
The power she was talking about wasn’t something to be gained, or fight for.
Violet already had it.

The dining hall was split in two. Downstairs for the regular students. Upstairs for the elites.
Four oversized thrones sat empty at the center of the upper platform.
Violet didn't need to ask who those belonged to.
After last night's dream — Asher's hands, his voice, the missing lock of hair — she was relieved those seats were empty.
Then the knot in her stomach tightened. If she was in the top twenty… did that mean she had to sit up there? With them?
"Earth to Violet!" Alice snapped her fingers. "The line's moving."
A girl waltzed past the entire line and started piling food onto a plate like she owned the place. Nobody said a word.
"That's Hope," Alice whispered. "Autumn's personal assistant."
Hope carried the tray upstairs and set it down in front of a girl with striking silver hair.
Autumn Carson.
As if she felt Violet staring, Autumn turned and locked eyes with her. The gaze felt like a challenge.
Violet didn't look away… until she felt Alice grab her arm.
"You're number twenty. Your spot's upstairs."
"I'll eat down here," Violet said, already walking toward a lower table.
The second she sat, the entire floor went silent.
Then Alice's panicked cry — "Violet, look out!"
Violet dodged just in time. Her breakfast crashed to the floor.
A girl stood over her, pure disgust twisting her features. "So this is who they replaced me with?"
Paige. The previous number twenty. The girl whose spot Violet had taken on the Lunaboard without even trying.
"She's sitting downstairs! She doesn't even know the rules!"
Phones came out. The cafeteria was watching.
Violet calmly brushed crumbs off her clothes and turned her back.
"Hey! I'm talking to you!" Paige shrieked. "Don't ignore me, you daughter of a whore."
That stopped Violet cold.
That word. The same word the girls at the audition had used. The same word that had followed her mother's name her entire life.
Something inside Violet snapped.
She turned. The storm in her eyes made Paige's smirk falter.
Paige swung. Violet caught her arm and twisted it behind her back.
Violet forced her to face the crowd.
"Listen up. I don't care who you are or what privileges you have at this school. Leave me alone, and we're good."
Her voice hardened. "And that word — 'whore' — don't ever use it around me."
"You're nothing but a whore, bitch," Paige spat.
Violet dragged her to the spilled food and shoved her face into the mess.
"Where I come from, we don't waste food," Violet said. "If it falls on the floor, you pick it up."
She let go. Paige sobbed into the wreckage.
Silence.
Then, from the elite section, slow clapping.
It spread. The whole cafeteria joined in.
But Violet felt no triumph. Only dread.
This wasn't applause. It was acceptance. Like this school kept testing her — and she kept passing tests she never signed up for.
Everyone clapped.
Except Autumn. She stared daggers at Violet.
And Violet realized something: every moment since that audition stage had been pulling her deeper. The acceptance letter. The Luna Board. The dream. And now this.
She wasn't climbing a ladder. She was being dragged toward something.
But what was it? Why was she really here? What was all this leading to?!
She bolted.
She had to find Principal Jameson and drop out of this nightmare. Today.
She ran straight for the administrative floor.
Straight for Principal Jameson.
She didn’t slow down. 
Didn’t hesitate.
This was ending now.
She knocked.
No answer.
She knocked again, wondering if Principal Jameson was even there. 
Frustrated, Violet turned to leave, then clearly heard, "Come in."
Her heart raced.
This was it. 
She'd walk in, demand they revoke her scholarship, and Principal Jameson would do it. 
Violet had made up her mind.
She walked in, heart pounding. 
She saw Principal Jameson sitting in her executive chair, back turned. 
For a second, Violet thought something looked different, like her build was bigger, but she shrugged it off, figuring it was just her imagination. 
Who else would be in the principal's chair?
Ignoring the weird feeling, Violet straightened up. 
She cleared her throat, gathering her courage....
“Principal Jameson, I need to talk to you.”
Principal Jameson didn't answer for over a minute. 
An awkward silence hung in the air.
 Figuring she might as well just come out with it, Violet dropped the bomb.
"I don't want to go to school here anymore, Principal Jameson. Please revoke my scholarship and give it to someone else."
There, it was out. 
Violet felt lighter, like a weight had been lifted. 
Now, there was no way the principal could ignore her.
The chair started to swivel.
Violet held her breath, but when the chair finally turned around, the face she saw made her blood run cold.
You have got to be kidding me!
It wasn't Principal Jameson, it was Asher freaking Nightshade sitting in her chair.
Asher stood, studying her.
“Tell me something, Violet. How did you do it?”
He took a slow step toward her.
“Last night…” His eyes darkened. “You pulled yourself out of my dream.”
He stopped in front of her.
“That has never happened,” Asher said quietly. “The only person who’s ever refused me. The only person powerful enough to resist a Cardinal Alpha… is supposedly a human with purple hair?”
Violet’s stomach dropped.
“That means you aren’t what you think you are. You’re not just some whore’s daughter, are you?”
Her jaw tightened.
“I don’t know where I came from,” Violet said sharply.
Asher smiled, slow and dangerous.
“That’s what makes this interesting.”
“Makes what interesting?” Violet asked, panic rising in her chest.
Asher began circling her. “One of us is supposed to marry Autumn. A real, honest-to-Gods she-wolf. So that we can breed pureblood Alpha heirs.”
The air between them tightened as he got closer.
“Autumn Carson has spent her whole life believing destiny belonged to her… just because she’s pureblood,” he said. “But the moment you resisted my command, that destiny changed.”
A faint smile curved his mouth. Another step.
“And once the other Cardinal Alphas realize what you are… they won’t let you go.”
Violet froze as Asher leaned even closer… Close enough to kiss.
“So I need to claim you before they do…”
Violet should have panicked. But once again she was seized by that same strange feeling, torn between fear and something primal.
“You, my purple queen,” he whispered, “are here to take Autumn’s place.”

I know. Above us, the solstice full moon rose higher and higher, bright and round. Everyone kept glancing up at it, waiting for the moment fate would pull mates together.

The scent deepened. Chocolate. Coffee.

Wolves laughing, crying, embracing as fate handed them the one person made for them. I watched, smiling politely because that was my job. Inside, something ached because I knew I'd never have a maid of my own.

The air between them tightened as he got closer.

They stared at each other with unsettled recognition.
