To Violet’s surprise, his eyes softened for a second, like he hadn’t meant to hurt her.
“Listen, purple girl, I don’t know what you and Roman are up to. But if you touch my stuff
again,
it won’t be good for anyone.”
His stuff? Oh, no. Violet realized he was the necklace’s owner. The green-haired guy
must have stolen it. That explained why he was running.
“Don’t get caught up in Roman’s games,” he warned before stalking off with the necklace.
Breathless and trembling, Violet had no idea what was going on. She just lay there,
humiliated and terrified.
Before she could move…
Another tall, imposing guy stood before her.
“Not again,” she thought.
He wore dark shades, which immediately set off Violet’s internal alarms.

Wait. Dark shades. Indoors.
Her blood went cold.
She knew those shades.
The audition. The stage. The questions that made her want to disappear.
It was him.
The Alpha who had humiliated her in front of every district.
The one she'd defied.
The one she couldn't stop thinking about, no matter how hard she tried.
Violet’s heart pounded, and a weird tingle ran through her, a warmth settling in her
stomach....
Behind those shades, she felt the weight of his gaze sizing her up, his eyes raked over
her body.
Suddenly, his lips twisted into a wild, unsettling grin.
“Welcome, my purple flower.”
Those words. "Purple flower."
A chill crawled down her spine.
She'd only said her name once, on that stage, under those lights. But he hadn't just
remembered it — he'd twisted it into something intimate. A pet name. Like he'd been rolling it
around in his mind ever since, savoring it, reshaping it into something that belonged to him.
Like he'd already claimed her.
And that meant he hadn't stopped thinking about her since the audition.
Then… high above them… The Luna Board stirred. A new name burned into the stone at
the very bottom of the list.
Number Twenty: Violet Purple.
Whispers and gasps all around.
The new girl… the strange one with purple hair and golden eyes… had already made the
Luna Board on her very first day.

The Alpha’s smile widened. Like he knew something she didn’t.
Violet’s fear spiked.
She ran. She didn’t look back. Not even once.
She tore through the halls of Lunaris at a full sprint.
Students flattened themselves against the walls as she passed.
Her pulse wouldn’t settle.
Her lungs burned.
Left. Right. Down a corridor she didn’t recognize.
She finally skidded to a stop when her legs refused to keep going.
Silence swallowed her.
No wolves. No whispers. No Luna Board.
Just her ragged breathing echoing off the walls.
“Get it together,” she muttered.
This wasn’t District One.
No one here knew how many times she’d been cornered in an alley.
No one here knew what it felt like to go to bed hungry.
To fight for space. To survive.
She’d handled worse than rich wolves with attitude problems.
Roman’s chaos. Griffin’s violence. Asher's obsession.
Three Cardinal Alphas in one day. And every single one of them had touched her life before
she'd even unpacked.
She straightened. “They don’t scare me,” she said under her breath.
A lie. But one she’d lived on before.

Footsteps approached.
“Wow,” a familiar voice said lightly. “You move fast for a new girl.”
Violet turned.
Alice stood at the end of the corridor, arms crossed, slightly breathless.
“You’ve been here ten minutes,” Alice continued, walking closer. “And you’ve already
collided with three Cardinal Alphas and triggered the Luna Board.”
Violet felt that familiar prickle crawl up her spine. “What does that mean?”
“It means,” Alice said carefully, “something is reacting to you.”
The word landed heavy.
Alice hesitated. Then, quieter:
“Principal Jameson is going to want to see you.”
“Why?”
“Because when the Luna Board moves unexpectedly…” Alice’s expression hardened.
“Lunaris notices.”
Violet’s throat went dry. “Great,” she muttered.
Alice leaned in close. "Violet… whatever happens in there, don't let Jameson make you
feel safe. She answers to the Alphas. Everyone here does."
It was the first time Alice's voice had lost its edge.
And that scared Violet more than anything.
Alice gestured down the hall.
“Come on. Before this gets worse.”
As she knocked Principal Jameson's office, a voice called out, "Come in."
She smiled as Violet walked in. "Welcome, Violet." But her smile faltered when she saw the
bruise marks on Viole's neck.
"Who did this to you?" she demanded, her voice full of worry.

For the first time since arriving, Violet felt a flicker of hope. Finally, someone was going to deal
with that jerk. She quickly explained what had happened, describing the red haired guy in detail.
But as she spoke, Principal Jameson's expression changed from anger to something much
worse: fear.
"You mean Griffin Hale did this to you?"
"Griffin Hale? Is that his name?" Violet asked.
"Yes, Miss Purple," Principal Jameson began, her voice suddenly cautious. “And you shouldn’t
be cavorting with him on your first day.”
She exhaled slowly, fingers tightening on the edge of her desk.
“There are… expectations here, Miss Purple.”
Violet frowned. “About what?”
Jameson hesitated.
“About who gets noticed. Who gets protected.”
Violet crossed her arms. “And who doesn’t.”
Jameson didn’t argue.
“Most of that attention is already spoken for,” she said carefully. “Bloodlines. Families. Girls who
were raised for this world.”
Violet looked up.
“There is one student in particular,” Jameson added. “A very special one…”
Viole's stomach tightened. "You're talking about Autumn Carson."
Jameson looked up, surprised. "You've heard the name."
"Hard not to. Everyone here says it like a prayer."
Jameson's voice lowered. "Then you understand what you're walking into."
"What I don't understand is why it involves me."
Jameson exhaled slowly.
"Because something reacted to you."
"Something?"

"One of them," she corrected. "Possibly more than one."
“And I’m guessing that’s not possible.”
Jameson’s expression darkened.
“It shouldn’t be.”
Silence stretched between them.
“If you are compatible with one of the Cardinal Alphas,” Jameson said carefully, “it changes
things.”
“For who?”
“For everyone.”
Violet swallowed.
“And if I’m not?”
Jameson’s eyes flicked briefly toward the window… toward the Academy beyond.
“Then today was a very dangerous coincidence.”
A knock at the door.
Alice poked her head in
“Alice, take Mrs. Purple to the Infirmary,” Jameson said quietly. “Get those marks treated.”
Violet turned to leave.
“Miss Purple.”
She paused.
“If the Luna Board moves again…”
Jameson’s voice dropped.
“Pray it’s only one of them.”
Violet swallowed hard and left with Alice for the infirmary.
As they walked through the gothic Lunaris corridors, Alice reached into her bag and handed
Violet a box.
“That’s your Lunaris welcome pack. Go ahead. Open it.”
Violet hesitated, then unzipped the bag. Textbooks. Supplies. And a sealed phone box.
Her breath caught.
“No way,” Violet whispered, lifting it out.
Alice smiled, all warmth again. “We give devices to scholarship students. Helps you stay
connected. Just log into the Lunaris Academy app. Campus Wi-Fi is everywhere.”
Violet turned the box over in her hands.
“Come on,” Alice said brightly, already moving again. “Let’s get you to the infirmary and have
those wounds checked.”
As Violet followed, phone still in her hand, the words of Principal Jameson wouldn’t leave her: “If
the Luna Board moves again… Pray it’s only one of them.”
Moments later, they entered the grand, impressive infirmary ward.
A healer, one of those super-rare werewolves who could do healing magic, was lecturing a
student… a guy whose arms were covered in fresh burns.
Violet barely registered the actual healer before her attention snapped to the guy.
“You can't keep doing this to yourself, Alaric,” the healer scolded.
"I'm fine," he grumbled, obviously annoyed, as the healer's magic soothed his burns.
Violet couldn’t be sure, but she thought she saw faint sparks crackle across his skin, dancing
like trapped lightning.
And she noticed that no one else stood close enough to touch him.
He must have felt Violet staring because he turned, and their eyes met.
Holy moly. Violet forgot to breathe. Her cheeks turned pink.
He had whitish-blond hair framing a face that was ridiculously good-looking.
But it was his eyes that really got her:

Stormy blue, like a gathering storm.
“That’s Alpha Alaric,” Alice whispered.
Great. Another Alpha. But this one seemed different somehow…
“No one can touch him,” Alice added.
“Why?” Violet asked.
Alice didn’t answer, but cryptically stared at the burn marks on his arms.
Violet studied him.
He had a quiet intensity, but instead of being cocky, there was an innocence about him that was
strangely attractive.
With those striking sapphire eyes, he could have easily been the most handsome alpha she'd
met today…
His gaze swept over her, head to toe, like he was checking her out, sending a surprising jolt
through her.
But just as quickly as that little flicker of excitement appeared, it was squashed by his sudden
cold, dismissive attitude.
His expression made it clear: he wasn't interested.
Any idea that he might have been was shattered by his icy indifference.
"You're good to go," the healer said, finishing up with him.
Done, Alaric brushed past Violet…
And in that quick, fleeting touch, a spark jolted through her.
It was like static shock, sharp, unexpected, and strangely exciting.
Violet froze, her breath catching in her throat…
Alaric stopped short.
He looked down at his hand.
Then at Violet.
Confusion flickered across his face… sharp, startled, unmistakable.

He touched her… and she was fine.
As if his lightning didn’t surge… but recoiled.
Like it had hit something it couldn’t burn through.
His storm didn’t harm Violet. It hesitated.
How?
For a split second, the storm in his eyes surged.
Then his expression slammed shut, colder than before.
Without a word, he turned and walked out.
Violet stood there, heart racing, skin still tingling.
“Did you see that?” Violet whispered.
Alice was staring at Alaric’s retreating back.
“That’s impossible,” Alice said under her breath.
“What is?” Violet demanded. “What just happened?”
Alice looked at her slowly.
“Alaric doesn’t touch people.”
“I noticed.”
“No,” Alice said, shaking her head. “You don’t understand. He can’t.”
Violet frowned.
“Alaric controls lightning. Not metaphorical lightning. Actual voltage. His body discharges
constantly. Static. Current. Storm build-up. That’s why no one stands near him.”
Violet looked down at her own hands.
“But he touched me.”
Alice nodded once.
“And you didn’t burn.”
Violet swallowed.

Silence settled between them.
“Why?” Violet asked.
Alice hesitated.
“The Cardinal Alphas aren’t like other wolves,” she said carefully. “They were born under a lunar
anomaly. People say the Moon Goddess gave them powers.”
She ticked them off quickly.
“Griffin has shockwave strength. He can level stone with a punch.”
“Roman is a Shapeshifter. Any animal. Total chaos.”
“Asher?” She lowered her voice. “Mind manipulation. Thoughts. Memories. Control.”
“And Alaric…” She glanced toward the door. “Storms. Lightning. Energy strong enough to
paralyze a room.”
Violet’s skin tingled again.
“So what does it mean that I’m, like, okay?”
Alice held her gaze.
“It means one of two things. Either you’re resistant to Alpha power… or you’re compatible with
it.”
The word hung between them.
Compatible.
Violet’s throat went dry.
“With him?” she asked quietly.
Alice didn’t answer right away.
“That’s the question,” she said.
Violet wondered what it all meant.
"You,” the healer interrupted. “What can I do for you?" the healer asked, her eyebrows furrowing
as she looked Violet over. "You're new here, aren't you?"
Violet nodded.

" And already in the infirmary on your first day?" The healer shook her head, clucking her
tongue.
"Good luck, kid."
"I know," Violet whispered, her voice barely there. "I know."
“It's nothing serious. You're good to go,” the healer said, handing her some painkillers, and then
Alice took Violet to the dorm rooms.
“Welcome to West House, Violet. This is your home now, and over there are the other houses:
East, South, and North.”
“Whoa!” Violet breathed, staring at the impressive buildings.
“Ms. Purple, you see, this school is all about hierarchy. Human or werewolf, everyone forms
packs in their houses. The four strongest cardinal alphas study here and run these four houses.
Everyone else follows their lead. They are basically gods here.”
Violet sighed. She had already seen the glimpses of student power on her very first day.
Alice continued, “The West House you are going to be in is run by Alpha Asher Nightshade.”
Violet's stomach clenched.
Of course it was.
Of all four houses, she'd been placed in his.
The Alpha who'd humiliated her on stage. The one who'd grinned at her in the hallway like he
owned her. The one who called her "purple flower" like it was already decided.
This wasn't random. It couldn't be.
“Don't worry,” Alice interrupted before Violet could ask. “Anything else? Everything you need to
know is on your phone, plus your roommates will fill you in. Go meet your roommates.”
As Violet entered her room, her roommates looked at her with surprising eyes.
"No way, it's really her," one of them said, sounding shocked.
Violet raised an eyebrow. Why did everyone at this school seem to know who she was?
"Hi, I'm Lily Fairchild," a girl chirped. "It's so nice to meet you, Violet Purple!"
Violet blinked, totally surprised by the sudden friendliness.

"The grumpy one over there is Hazel Sterling," Alice said, pointing to another blonde who
looked permanently scowling.
When their eyes met, Violet immediately felt the dislike radiating from Hazel.
Alice leaned in closer to Violet. "Hazel's just jealous of you."
Violet frowned. "What do you mean she's jealous of me?" she asked Alice, then turned to Hazel.
"No offense, but we literally just met. Why would you be jealous of me? That makes zero
sense."
“Offense taken!” Hazel said.
“Oh, really, Hazel? Seriously? Your ego is out of control, especially after you were just gossiping
about that video,” Lily finally chimed in.
“What video?” Violet asked
All three girls turned to her, looking at her like she was totally clueless.
“You haven't checked your newsfeed,” Lily said.
"Newsfeed?" Violet echoed, even more confused.
“BioDome,” Lily explained. “It's where everyone at Lunaris Academy gets all the school news.
And yeah, you're kinda trending right now.”
Before she could even grab her phone to search for this BioDome thing, Alice had hers out.
Alice searched for the video using Violet's name, and there it was.
Violet's eyes widened as the video started playing.
It was a clip of Griffin manhandling her.
“Oh, God! Who the hell got...”
As she watched herself, awkward and vulnerable, the thought that the entire school had seen
her like that burned in her chest.
“Gods, you’re so lucky,” Hazel sneered from her bed.
“Lucky?!” Violet shook her head, exasperated. ""What are you talking about? What's so special
about these guys that everyone's losing their minds?"
"The Terror Four," Lily answered with a wry smile. “Most of us would kill to even be seen by
them! But unfortunately, only those ranked between first and twentieth have their attention."

Violet’s stomach tightened.
She thought about the green-haired thief.
The red-haired brute.
The one with lightning under his skin.
And Asher…. The obsessive one.
This wasn’t coincidence. This felt like gravity. Forced proximity.
As if her life hadn’t started today by accident, but on schedule.
As if she hadn’t come to Lunaris to learn about the Cardinal Alphas…
But to change them.
“So,” Alice grinned. “Any Alpha you like?”
“What?” Violet blinked.
“You’re in the top twenty now,” Lily said. “They’ll see you as an equal.”
But Hazel scoffed. “Please. They’re all practically taken.”
“Yeah, but no one’s officially Luna yet,” Alice shot back.
Hazel’s smile turned sharp. “Don’t kid yourself. Autumn’s already been raised for that crown.”
Violet stiffened. “Autumn.”
For a split second, her mind traced back to Principal Jameson’s office…
“There is one student in particular,” Jameson had said. “Her name is Autumn.”
Hazel continued. “Number one. Never challenged. And she doesn’t lose.”
Autumn was the girl Lunaris had been preparing for.
The one everyone assumed would be chosen.
The one the rules were built around.
What none of them knew yet…
Was that Violet, the strange purple-haired girl standing in front of them, wasn’t meant to follow
that rule.

She was meant to break it.
For now, Violet's patience finally snapped. "All right, enough! It’s not like I am even interested."
She looked each of them in the eye. "I'm so sick of the ridiculous drama at this school!"
Violet's roommates were speechless. A heavy silence filled the room.
Violet didn't wait for any response. Turning her back to them, she lay down on her bed and
closed her eyes, shutting them out. Sleep came quickly, her body exhausted and her mind still
buzzing from the day's craziness.
That night, Violet’s life changed!
Violet stirred in her sleep. Strong arms wrapped around her. A face buried into her purple hair.
It felt so good she instinctively snuggled closer. His scent was intoxicating. And somehow
familiar…
Then she opened her eyes.
She was back on the stage of the audition. No other girls. No audience. No cameras.
Just her. And Asher.
No. This had to be a dream. He was in her head.
Alice's warning crashed through her mind: He can plant thoughts, erase memories — basically
puppet-master you.
This was his power. And she was trapped inside it.
She broke free from his hold and stumbled back.
"Is this my dream?"
"I might be in your head, but this feels pretty real to me." His voice dropped to a low whisper.
"And it could be real for you, too. If you let me."
Something in Violet's blood reacted… humming, answering him before her mind could stop it.
"Where's my body?" she snapped.
"Your body's in your room. Your mind's here with me."
The scene shimmered. Shifted.
When Violet blinked, she was straddling Asher on a bed in a room she'd never seen before.
Black stone walls. Candlelight. The air thick with incense.
His world. His rules.
She tried to move, but she couldn’t.
"Calm down, baby," he murmured.
Violet's skin crawled. She was disgusted by him. But her body wouldn't cooperate.
That pull was back. Stronger. Insistent.
As if her blood recognized him… even as her mind rebelled.
He looked at her with that dark, hungry gaze. Like he wanted to swallow her whole. Like he'd
been waiting for her forever.
"Be mine, my purple flower," he said. "Be my queen. Rule with me."
"Let me go!" she spat.
"You're the only one who can talk to me like that and get away with it," Asher said. "Do you
know how rare that is?"
"If you want to kill me, just do it. I'm not begging."
"Why would I kill my queen?"
Why was he so obsessed with her? What was it about her that he couldn't resist?
It was the same question she'd had on that stage. The same look in his eyes when she'd
refused his Command. Like she was something impossible. Something he had to have.
"I'm done here," Violet snarled. "Send me back. Now."
"Sure thing," Asher replied smoothly. "But first, I need a little something to remember you by."
Scissors—then, a soft snip echoed in the silence.
A lock of her purple hair rested in his palm.
"You!" Violet exploded.

And just like at the audition — when his Command had tried to break her and failed —
something inside Violet surged.
Not anger. Not fear.
Power.
The dream cracked. The candlelight flickered wild. Asher's grin faltered for the first time.
"What are you—"
She didn't let him finish. She tore herself out of his world like ripping through a wall.
Violet woke with a gasp.
Sweat soaked her sheets. Her heart was racing like she’d been running for her life.
For a second, she thought it had all been a dream.
Asher.
His hands. His voice in her head.
She stumbled into the bathroom, gripping the sink, staring at her reflection.
Her clothes were untouched. Her body unharmed.
Relief hit her…
Then her hand went to her hair.
A chunk was missing.
Violet froze.
Her fingers traced the jagged edge where purple strands should have been.
Her stomach dropped.
It wasn’t a dream.
Asher Nightshade had been inside her head.
And he’d taken something with him.
“I need to get out of this place,” she whispered.

That thought hardened instantly.
Lunaris Academy was a trap.
And she decided right then and there…
She wasn’t going to stay long enough to find out what else it could take from her.
Morning came too fast.
Alice burst into the room like nothing had happened, all cheer and chatter, while Violet dressed
in silence.
The Lunaris Academy uniform fit perfectly. Too perfectly. Like it had been made for her.
Alice noticed the tension immediately.
The way Violet’s shoulders stayed tight. The way her eyes never quite settled, always alert.
Her smile softened.
Alice stepped closer, fixing Violet’s tie for her, hands steady… deliberate.
Protective.
“Listen, Violet,” Alice said quietly. “Power is the only currency here. If you want to be left alone,
you need it.”
Violet didn’t answer.
She didn’t want power. She wanted out.
Alice held her gaze a moment longer than necessary.
As if making a silent promise.
Because Alice knew something Violet didn’t yet… She knew the secret.
The power she was talking about wasn’t something to be gained, or fight for.
Violet already had it.
The dining hall was split in two. Downstairs for the regular students. Upstairs for the elites.
Four oversized thrones sat empty at the center of the upper platform.

Violet didn't need to ask who those belonged to.
After last night's dream — Asher's hands, his voice, the missing lock of hair — she was relieved
those seats were empty.
Then the knot in her stomach tightened. If she was in the top twenty… did that mean she had to
sit up there? With them?
"Earth to Violet!" Alice snapped her fingers. "The line's moving."
A girl waltzed past the entire line and started piling food onto a plate like she owned the place.
Nobody said a word.
"That's Hope," Alice whispered. "Autumn's personal assistant."
Hope carried the tray upstairs and set it down in front of a girl with striking silver hair.
Autumn Carson.
As if she felt Violet staring, Autumn turned and locked eyes with her. The gaze felt like a
challenge.
Violet didn't look away… until she felt Alice grab her arm.
"You're number twenty. Your spot's upstairs."
"I'll eat down here," Violet said, already walking toward a lower table.
The second she sat, the entire floor went silent.
Then Alice's panicked cry — "Violet, look out!"
Violet dodged just in time. Her breakfast crashed to the floor.
A girl stood over her, pure disgust twisting her features. "So this is who they replaced me with?"
Paige. The previous number twenty. The girl whose spot Violet had taken on the Lunaboard
without even trying.
"She's sitting downstairs! She doesn't even know the rules!"
Phones came out. The cafeteria was watching.
Violet calmly brushed crumbs off her clothes and turned her back.
"Hey! I'm talking to you!" Paige shrieked. "Don't ignore me, you daughter of a whore."
That stopped Violet cold.

That word. The same word the girls at the audition had used. The same word that had followed
her mother's name her entire life.
Something inside Violet snapped.
She turned. The storm in her eyes made Paige's smirk falter.
Paige swung. Violet caught her arm and twisted it behind her back.
Violet forced her to face the crowd.
"Listen up. I don't care who you are or what privileges you have at this school. Leave me alone,
and we're good."
Her voice hardened. "And that word — 'whore' — don't ever use it around me."
"You're nothing but a whore, bitch," Paige spat.
Violet dragged her to the spilled food and shoved her face into the mess.
"Where I come from, we don't waste food," Violet said. "If it falls on the floor, you pick it up."
She let go. Paige sobbed into the wreckage.
Silence.
Then, from the elite section, slow clapping.
It spread. The whole cafeteria joined in.
But Violet felt no triumph. Only dread.
This wasn't applause. It was acceptance. Like this school kept testing her — and she kept
passing tests she never signed up for.
Everyone clapped.
Except Autumn. She stared daggers at Violet.
And Violet realized something: every moment since that audition stage had been pulling her
deeper. The acceptance letter. The Luna Board. The dream. And now this.

She wasn't climbing a ladder. She was being dragged toward something.
But what was it? Why was she really here? What was all this leading to?!
She bolted.
She had to find Principal Jameson and drop out of this nightmare. Today.
She ran straight for the administrative floor.
Straight for Principal Jameson.
She didn’t slow down.
Didn’t hesitate.
This was ending now.
She knocked.
No answer.
She knocked again, wondering if Principal Jameson was even there.
Frustrated, Violet turned to leave, then clearly heard, "Come in."
Her heart raced.
This was it.
She'd walk in, demand they revoke her scholarship, and Principal Jameson would do it.
Violet had made up her mind.
She walked in, heart pounding.
She saw Principal Jameson sitting in her executive chair, back turned.
For a second, Violet thought something looked different, like her build was bigger, but she
shrugged it off, figuring it was just her imagination.
Who else would be in the principal's chair?
Ignoring the weird feeling, Violet straightened up.
She cleared her throat, gathering her courage....

“Principal Jameson, I need to talk to you.”
Principal Jameson didn't answer for over a minute.
An awkward silence hung in the air.
Figuring she might as well just come out with it, Violet dropped the bomb.
"I don't want to go to school here anymore, Principal Jameson. Please revoke my scholarship
and give it to someone else."
There, it was out.
Violet felt lighter, like a weight had been lifted.
Now, there was no way the principal could ignore her.
The chair started to swivel.
Violet held her breath, but when the chair finally turned around, the face she saw made her
blood run cold.
You have got to be kidding me!
It wasn't Principal Jameson, it was Asher freaking Nightshade sitting in her chair.
Asher stood, studying her.
“Tell me something, Violet. How did you do it?”
He took a slow step toward her.
“Last night…” His eyes darkened. “You pulled yourself out of my dream.”
He stopped in front of her.
“That has never happened,” Asher said quietly. “The only person who’s ever refused me. The
only person powerful enough to resist a Cardinal Alpha… is supposedly a human with purple
hair?”
Violet’s stomach dropped.
“That means you aren’t what you think you are. You’re not just some whore’s daughter, are
you?”
Her jaw tightened.
“I don’t know where I came from,” Violet said sharply.

Asher smiled, slow and dangerous.
“That’s what makes this interesting.”
“Makes what interesting?” Violet asked, panic rising in her chest.
Asher began circling her. “One of us is supposed to marry Autumn. A real, honest-to-Gods she-
wolf. So that we can breed pureblood Alpha heirs.”
The air between them tightened as he got closer.
“Autumn Carson has spent her whole life believing destiny belonged to her… just because she’s
pureblood,” he said. “But the moment you resisted my command, that destiny changed.”
A faint smile curved his mouth. Another step.
“And once the other Cardinal Alphas realize what you are… they won’t let you go.”
Violet froze as Asher leaned even closer… Close enough to kiss.
“So I need to claim you before they do…”
Violet should have panicked. But once again she was seized by that same strange feeling, torn
between fear and something primal.
“You, my purple queen,” he whispered, “are here to take Autumn’s place.”
Asher wants Violet to take Autumn's place. But Autumn has never lost… how far will she
go to protect what's hers?
Four Cardinal Alphas. Four divine powers. And not one of them could break Violet. So
what happens when they all want her?
Something ancient is hiding in Violet’s blood. Something that terrifies the most powerful
wolves alive. What is she?

Hey, it's a living, kind of.\n \nThey forced me to stay in the packhouse dungeon with nothing but a cot, a cracked washbasin, and one blanket that smelled like mildew and regret. Home sweet dungeon. And tomorrow night, while every beautiful she-wolf in the pack dressed in silk and waited for fate to choose her, I would attend the mating ball too, as the servant carrying their wine.\n \nThe night before the ball, I was summoned to Princess Marcy's chambers, the cruel pack princess, my greatest tormentor, cunning, beautiful, vicious. Hold still, mutt. She sneered, driving a dress pin into my wrist.\n \nI bit the inside of my cheek and kept my eyes on the marble floor. Do not scream. Screaming only made it worse.\n \nMarcy stood on a raised platform in front of three golden mirrors, her blonde hair shining down her back, her mouth painted rose pink, her eyes cold and pleased with themselves. Her expensive gown clung to her body like it had been bullied into submission. Silver silk, diamond beading, a long train, basically everything I would never touch unless I was being forced to bleed on it.\n \nNora, Marcy's best friend, knelt beside the hem with a handful of pins and a smile that made me believe she had been a hyena in a past life. Leasley's growl filled my chest.\n \nMy hand snapped around Marcy's wrist. The room trembled. What was happening to me? Could I really be more than I knew? No more.\n \nI commanded in a voice that was only half my own. Marcy's eyes widened. What? I rose.\n \nThe dagger clattered to the floor. I am done, I said, my voice shaking, but mine. I am done being your toy.\n \nMarcy stared at me, at my face, at my pulsing silver eyes. For one horrible second, I thought she understood. Then her lip curled, fear twisting into disgust.\n \nWhat's wrong with your eyes? She snapped. Are you sick or something? Before I could answer, horns blared outside. The dark howlers would be arriving any minute.\n \nDamon would be arriving. Marcy's fear twisted into panic. She backed toward the door.\n \nThis isn't over. It never is, I whispered. She fled.\n \nI ran until I found air. The roof, the one place in the packhouse where no one looked for me, unless they wanted to shove me off something. I stumbled to the edge, chest heaving, hands shaking.\n \nBelow, the packhouse grounds were exploding into movement. Servants ran, guards lined the drive, banners snapped in the wind. Inside me, Leasley flickered.\n \nWeakly, too weakly. Leasley? Her voice came soft. I used too much.\n \nPanic punched through me. What does that mean? My time is almost up. No.\n \nWhen the full moon reaches its peak tonight, Leasley whispered, I will fade away, my girl. The world tilted. I pressed both hands to my chest.\n \nNo, you just got here. I can't go back, I said, my voice breaking. I can't go back to being empty.\n \nWind whipped my hair across my face. My eyes burned. I looked over the edge of the roof.\n \nFour stories down, stone courtyard. A quick end, maybe. If Leasley vanished, if Marcy owned me, if Edward killed me, if Damon chose Marcy and everything got worse, what was left? Talia, Leasley said sharply.\n \nI can't do this without you. You can, and you will. I don't want to.\n \nSilence, then warmth, faint but fierce, wrapped around my heart. I will return one day, Leasley said. When you need me most, I need you now.\n \nUntil, you mustn't tell anyone about me, or they will try to sever us forever, she continued. For you are more than you know, Talia. Tonight, fate begins.\n \nAll will be revealed when the full moon peaks. Your true power will begin to awaken when he arrives. What did she mean? What power could I, a worthless runt, possibly have? What plan did fate have in store for me? Who was he? And what, exactly, was he supposed to unlock? Leasley's voice faded.\n \nPromise me you will hold on for one more night. I stared over the edge. Finally, I whispered.\n \nFine. One more night. Warmth spread through me.\n \nThe sting at my collarbone faded. I looked down. Marcy's carved initials dissolved from my skin.\n \nIn their place, a tiny crescent moon glowed softly over my collarbone. I touched it, stunned. Then the moonlight shifted.\n \nSilver radiance spilled through the clouds and wrapped around me. My torn work smock shimmered. The fabric mended itself, until I stood in a simple gown of pale silver, delicate as moonlight, beautiful in a way that made my throat ache.\n \nI stared down at myself. Leasley. Her voice smiled.\n \nYou can't go to a ball without a gown. How did you... The moon goddess provides. Below, engines purred.\n \nBlack cars rolled through the gates, sleek and dark as wolves in shadow. The dark howlers had arrived. I gripped the roof's edge and looked down as guards opened the doors.\n \nMy heart slammed. The mating ball was upon us. One more night, I told myself.\n \nI only had to hold on for one more night. What did fate have in store? What would happen at the full moon's peak? Downstairs, the mating ball had officially begun. Silver garlands draped from the chandeliers.\n \nMoonflowers climbed the pillars. Crystal goblets sparkled on every table. The entire ballroom glowed beneath the solstice moonlight spilling through the glass ceiling above.\n \nTonight the silver moon will rise to weave our fate across the skies. A full heart will pray for destiny to find its way. Candles glow.\n \nThe violins sing. Moonflowers bloom as dancers spin. The grandest night the wolves have known to find the soul that's called their own.\n \nYet one small heart still dares to dream. Perhaps tonight fate waits for me. The ancient bond will soon ignite and every life will change tonight.\n \nI moved through the crowd with a tray balanced on one hand, offering mushroom tarts, honeyed figs, and tiny lamb skewers to noble wolves who looked right through me. That was fine. Being ignored was one of my better talents.\n \nInside my chest, Liesli stirred. Barely. Her warmth had been fading all evening, thinning with every inch the moon climbed higher in the sky.\n \nLiesli? I whispered, keeping my smile fixed as a she-wolf snatched two tarts without saying thank you. I'm here, she said softly. But she sounded far away.\n \nToo far. My fingers tightened around the tray. You're fading.\n \nI know. Above us, the solstice full moon rose higher and higher, bright and round. Everyone kept glancing up at it, waiting for the moment fate would pull mates together.\n \nBut what fate was waiting for me? What was supposed to happen when the moon finally peaked? Could I truly be more than the lowly runt everyone had always told me I was? And who was this mysterious man Liesli claimed would unlock it? I slipped outside to deliver a tray of drinks to the terrace, mostly because I needed one second where no one was sneering at me over a stuffed mushroom. The terrace overlooked the front drive, where black cars lined the courtyard. Dark howlers.\n \nEven their cars looked daunting and expensive. Near the stone railing, a group of she-wolves huddled together, whispering and giggling. Nora was in the middle of them, of course.\n \nShe wore red silk and enough perfume to stun a battlefield. I heard he killed three rogues with his bare hands. One girl whispered, I heard he rejected an alpha's daughter because she smiled too much.\n \nAnother said, Nora fanned herself. I heard he's even more handsome up close. You saw him? Only for a second, Nora said.\n \nBut goddess, alpha daemon is... unreal. They all sighed. I tried to step around them, but Nora spotted me.\n \nHer gaze flicked over my tray. Oh look, the kitchen rat is delivering refreshments. I lowered my eyes.\n \nWould you like one? Not if your hands touched it. The rich girls laughed. I was used to it.\n \nThen the air changed, and the girls went silent. A scent rolled across the terrace. Rich.\n \nDark. Warm. Coffee and chocolate and smoke after rain.\n \nMy breath caught. Liesli lifted her head inside me so sharply it hurt. Across the courtyard below, a tall figure stepped from the shadows.\n \nAlpha daemon. I saw him only for a moment. Dark hair, broad shoulders, a black suit that hugged his muscled frame.\n \nEven from far away, power clung to him like a storm about to break. The she-wolves around me practically melted into the stone. For one strange heartbeat, daemon turned his head toward the terrace.\n \nThe scent deepened. Chocolate. Coffee.\n \nDanger. Then daemon disappeared back inside, and Liesli went quiet. Later, I stood along the side of the ballroom with a tray of bacon-wrapped dates and watched the wolves dance.\n \nThe moon was nearly at its peak now. Everyone could feel it. The air buzzed.\n \nCouples kept pausing mid-step, glancing around as if their souls had started tugging on invisible strings. A girl near the musicians gasped and dropped her fan. Across the room, a young warrior froze.\n \nTheir eyes met. The whole room erupted into cheers as he crossed to her, shaking, and whispered something I couldn't hear. Another bond sparked near the punch table, then another by the balcony doors.\n \nWolves laughing, crying, embracing as fate handed them the one person made for them. I watched, smiling politely because that was my job. Inside, something ached because I knew I'd never have a maid of my own.\n \nSomeone who would see you once and know. Someone who would cross a room for you. Someone who would never let Marcy touch you again.\n \nBut who would ever choose a lowly Omega runt like myself? Liesli stirred faintly. Don't look so sad. I'm not sad, I whispered.\n \nI'm holding bacon-wrapped dates. You are terrible at lying. Just then, a woman stepped beside me and plucked an appetizer from the tray.\n \nMaya. I recognized her from reputation. The mate of Alpha Damon's beta.\n \nDark hair, sharp eyes, a rose and dagger tattoo on her forearm. She chewed thoughtfully, then brightened. Oh, this is delicious.\n \nI blinked. Thank you, ma'am. What an amazing cook you are.\n \nI was so unused to kindness that I almost looked behind me to see who she meant. Maya's gaze softened as she studied my face. What's your name? Talia.\n \nTalia. She repeated. Are you always this small? I stiffened.\n \nI try not to take up too much space. Her mouth tightened. That's not what I meant.\n \nHer eyes moved over me, my thin wrists, my hollow cheeks. The faint bruising Liesli hadn't had enough strength to fully heal. Is this how Red Moon treats its Omegas? She asked quietly.\n \nMy stomach dropped. Before I could answer, a tall man stepped up beside her. Caden, Damon's beta.\n \nHe looked calmer than most of the Dark Howlers, which was to say he looked like he could politely remove someone's head if asked. He said, then glanced at me. His gaze sharpened for half a second.\n \nI lowered my eyes. Maya touched his arm. Any sign of what's bothering Damon? Caden exhaled.\n \nNo, but he's been strange since we arrived. Restless, distracted, like something is driving him mad. My pulse picked up.\n \nOr someone, Maya said. Caden's eyes flicked toward the moonlit ceiling. The Solstice can do strange things.\n \nDo you think he found her? Maya asked softly. His mate? My fingers tightened around the tray. Could it be Marcy? She asked.\n \nI shuddered at the thought. I don't know. Caden said.\n \nBut something is happening. Caden's eyes turned toward me, slow, assessing. Why was he staring at me? Before anyone could ask another question, a howl erupted through the ballroom, deep, primal, then another, and another.\n \nThe full moon had reached its peak. The ballroom exploded. Wolves cried out as bonds ignited.\n \nSome laughed, some sobbed, some dropped to their knees. The mating ball had truly begun. Maya grabbed Caden's hand.\n \nWe need to find Damon. Caden nodded, but his gaze lingered on me one second too long. Then they disappeared into the crowd.\n \nInside my chest, Leasley flickered like a dying candle. Talia, she whispered. My throat tightened.\n \nNo. It's time. No.\n \nYou said soon. This isn't soon. This is now.\n \nI will come back when you need me most. I need you now. Her warmth wrapped around my heart one last time.\n \nRemember what I told you, my girl. You are more than we know. Trust me.\n \nAll will be revealed soon. Leasley. We will meet again.\n \nThen she faded. The space inside me went quiet. Too quiet.\n \nLike a room after the last candle goes out. I swallowed hard, blinking fast. No.\n \nNot here. Not now. How could I go on without Leasley? What did fate have planned for me? And who was the mysterious man meant to unlock it? I looked across the ballroom, desperate to focus on anything else.\n \nThat was when I noticed Alpha Edward near the high table. His gaze was sharp and fixed directly on me. His earlier threat slammed back into my skull.\n \nIf Marcy did not end this night bonded to Damon, it would be my head. I scanned the ballroom, the dancers, the laughing she-wolves, the moonlit corners. Marcy was gone.\n \nMy blood turned cold. Oh, that was bad. That was very, very bad.\n \nI set the tray down and ran. I checked the powder room, the dressing room, the side parlor. All empty.\n \nMy panic climbed with every door. Where was she? If Marcy was late to her own destiny, Alpha Edward would not blame Marcy. He would blame the disposable handmaiden.\n \nMe. I raced upstairs to Marcy's chambers and pressed my ear to the door. Nothing.\n \nNo voices. No movement. Then I heard a sound from down the hall.\n \nA low murmur. A breath. From the guest room.\n \nI crept toward the sound and stopped outside the largest guest room, Alpha Damon's room. My body went cold. I knocked lightly.\n \nNo answer. I pushed the door open. I froze.\n \nMarcy was on her knees in front of Alpha Damon. Her hands were on his belt. His expression was hard.\n \nHis jaw tight. His body rigid. I had just walked in on the most powerful Alpha in the realm, being seduced by the pack princess I was supposed to be supervising.\n \nI gasped. Damon's head snapped toward me. His eyes locked onto mine.\n \nIce blue. Piercing. His scent hit me full force.\n \nCoffee. Chocolate. Danger.\n \nMy knees nearly gave out. Marcy whipped around. Talia? I did the only thing I could.\n \nI turned and ran. Wait! Damon barked. Oh, goddess.\n \nHe was going to kill me. I barely made it into the hall before a hand caught my wrist. The world spun.\n \nMy back hit the wall. Damon pinned me there. One hand braced beside my head.\n \nThe other locked around my wrist. He was huge. Warm.\n \nClose. Too close. His scent wrapped around me until I could barely think.\n \nWas this how I died? I wished for Lieselie so hard it hurt. Damon leaned closer. His eyes searched my face like he was trying to remember me from a dream.\n \nYou. He breathed. I swallowed.\n \nMe? A low growl rumbled from his chest. Not angry. Hungry.\n \nPossessive. Terrifying. Then Marcy stormed into the hall.\n \nWhat the hell is this? Damon did not move away from me. Marcy's eyes went from his hand on my wrist to my body trapped against the wall. Her face twisted.\n \nYou little thief. I didn't. The dagger from before flashed in Marcy's hand before I saw it coming.\n \nPain tore through my side. I looked down. Marcy's blade was buried inside me.\n \nFor one second, I stared at it like it belonged to someone else. Then she yanked it free. Blood spilled hot over my dress.\n \nI gasped, knees buckling. Damon's growl shook the hallway. The sound made the torches flicker.\n \nHe turned on Marcy, eyes blazing. Do not touch her. Why was he so angry? Why did he care that Marcy had hurt me? Why did he care about a wolfless runt? Damon grabbed Marcy's wrist, twisting it until she dropped the blade.\n \nHe threw her back against the wall. Then George appeared at the end of the hall. His eyes locked on Marcy.\n \nOn Damon. Something broken and furious twisted across his face. With a roar, he charged.\n \nDamon moved fast. He caught George by the throat and threw him sideways into the wall like he was nothing. Stone cracked.\n \nGeorge collapsed. Guards shouted. Doors burst open.\n \nRed moon warriors flooded the hallway. Protect the princess! Seize him! Help for Damon! Caden and Maya appeared from the stairwell, pushing through the chaos. Damon snarled as guards tackled him.\n \nThree wolves hit him at once. He threw one off, then another. The hallway became a blur of bodies, growls, fists, and flashing claws.\n \nNo one looked at me. For once, being invisible helped. I pressed a hand to my bleeding side and slid down the wall.\n \nLeasley, I whispered. Nothing. Leasley, please.\n \nBlood soaked through my fingers. My head swam. I crawled.\n \nOne arm forward, then the other. Away from the shouting. Away from Marcy.\n \nAway from Damon. My vision blurred. The floor tilted.\n \nI left a trail of blood behind me. Too much blood. Then the world dimmed.\n \nThe last thing I saw was the moonlight stretching across the hallway floor. The last thing I felt was the hollow ache where Leasley used to be. And then, I passed out cold.\n \nI didn't hear Damon throw off the guards. I didn't hear the roar that silenced the hall. I didn't hear his voice tear through the packhouse.\n \nWhere is she? Someone answered, trembling. Where is who, Alpha Damon? Damon's roar shook the walls. Where is my mate? Is it possible? Is Talia truly Damon's fated mate? What will Damon do to protect her? now","cards":[],"body":{"text":"Violet stood outside in the cold, trying to sell the last of her wares.\nPeople walked past without slowing down.\n\nAcross the road, through the lit window of the diner on Fifth, she could see a booth of girls her age \u2014 laughing, leaning into each other, splitting a plate of fries.\nFor a moment, Violet just stood there, watching. Because once, she used to think that could be her too.\nBut all of that stopped the night she understood what she was. The girl nobody wanted. The one Nancy found in the trash.\n\nOne moment she was just a kid.\n\nThe next, she was a label.\n\nFrom that day on, Violet learned how to take up less space.\n\nHow to keep her head down.\n\nHow to make sure no one looked too long.\nShe was eighteen now.\n\nNo pack. No bloodline. No wolf.\n\nThat meant exactly one thing \u2014\nshe was on her own.\nForever.\n\nEvery day someone found a new way to remind her.\nShe endured it because she had no other choice.\n\nEvery day someone found a new way to remind her.\nShe endured it because she had no other choice.\nBut it all reached a tipping point the night two Lunaris guards cornered her in a dark alley.\n\u201cHand it over.\u201d\nShe didn't argue. She never argued.\nShe stuck her hand out and held out with everything she had \u2014 twelve dollars...\nThe guard knocked it from her grip and laughed.\n\u201cWhy'd you do that?\u201d\n\n\u201cBecause there ain't a thing you can do about it, purple.\u201d\nThe two guards were still chuckling as they turned to leave. And then Violet felt something she had never felt before.\nHer hair began to glow \u2014 deep violet light bleeding through every strand.\nWhat the hell is she?\nGet the car. We're taking her in.\nTaking her where?\nThe Luna audition.\nTwenty girls from every district had been invited to Lunaris Academy. One exclusive audition. One chance to become the future Luna of a Cardinal Alpha. Every girl looked like she belonged\u2026 except Violet.\nGolden eyes.\nPurple hair.\nSecond-hand clothes.\nShe stood out like a pigeon among doves.\nViolet never wanted this audition.\nWith every district watching live, she knew she'd become the joke of the night.\nHow could a dirt-poor girl possibly become an alpha's bride? Violet was never supposed to be here. She never aspired to become a Luna. \n\nWhen she heard that the auditions would be filmed and broadcast live to all the districts, she'd done everything she could to avoid them. She knew that if she went up on stage with all the district's most beautiful girls, she would be humiliated. She'd done everything she could to avoid the audition.\nBut minutes before it began, the school bullies cornered her.\nWith her tights ripped, her shirt soaked and her beanie torn off \u2026 Violet was shoved through the gym doors. \n\"Let the alphas see what trash you really are,\" \n\nA spotlight flicked on at center court, and Violet stumbled straight into it. Laughter rippled through the bleachers. The bullies didn't just want her embarrassed, they wanted her displayed. Violet turned to run, but it was too late. \n\n\"The show starts in 5,\"  a wolf guard declared.  \"Get ready for the cardinal alpha to make his appearance.\" \n\nExcited whispers and squeals filled the stage. The girls began to gossip to each other. \nUh, I hope it's Alaric. It doesn't matter. Autumn's gonna be chosen no matter what. This audition is just for show. \n\nViolet frowned. \n\n\"Who's Autumn?\" \nEvery girl near her looked at Violet like she'd just asked what the sun was. \n\n\u201cUp there!\u201d\nOne of them said, nodding toward a private viewing box above the bleachers. Violet followed her gaze. A girl with striking silver hair sat alone, watching the stage below. \nAutumn Carson. The girl every Cardinal Alpha wanted.\nShe wasn't here to audition. She was here to judge the competition. The alphas don't pick their Luna. She picks which alpha she wants. She's just here to size up her competition. \nPanic rose in Violet's chest. \"I shouldn't be here.\"\nThe guard grabbed her arm. \"Your job is to please the alpha.\"\n\"Refuse... and I'll throw you to the wolves.\"\nViolet followed his gaze to the other guards standing around the auditorium. \nShe shuddered. She had no choice but to play this cruel game.\n\nA collective gasp filled the stage as the back doors flew open. The room fell so silent she could hear a pin drop. \n\nViolet looked up, and her breath caught. A single man stood framed in a halo of light. He was tall and handsome with black hair and dark sunglasses. His smile was sharp, predatory, undeniably dangerous: Alpha Asher Nightshade. \n\nAlpha Asher Nightshade. One of the four Cardinal Alphas.\nCold. Untouchable.\nEvery girl wanted him. He wanted none of them. Students whispered that he was carved from stone.  Every girl straightened as he passed.  Asher didn't look at a single one of them. \nViolet was the only girl in the room who didn't know who Asher was. She didn't care. She refused to let some snobby, entitled alpha get under her skin. \n\nBut every time she looked at him, something underneath her skin tingled. Asher didn't bother with introductions. He took the only chair on the stage and spoke in a clear, cold voice that left no room for questions. \n\nAll right, girls, let's cut to the chase. Tonight, you belong to me. You answer my questions, you obey my commands. If I like what I hear or see, \n\nI'll consider making one of you my girlfriend. Let's begin with the girl in the red dress. \n\nStep up and state your name and district. \n\nThe girl next to Violet strode forward with a big, wide smile. \nI'm Maddie from District Three. \n\nTell me, Maddie,  how many guys have you made out with? \n\nThe girl's mouth dropped open in disbelief. A hush fell over the room. Every eye shifted to her. The way Asher stayed silent made Violet shiver. \n\n\u201cThat's it. Leave, now. \u201c\n\nAnd a shudder went through the girl's body, because this was an alpha command, an ironclad instruction that forces all humans and wolves to obey. The girl's pupils dilated as the command took hold.  She turned around robotically and walked out the gym, moving stiffly like a puppet on strings. This was an alpha's ability. It was like they saw these girls as toys, and this was their game. \n\nViolet couldn't see Asher\u2019s eyes behind those sunglasses, but she could feel his gaze slide over her- \nYou with the purple hair, \nyou're up next. \n\nAs soon as Violet reached the center of the stage, the alpha began. \n\"Name?\"\n\"Violet Purple.\"\n\"What's your type?\"\n\"Like my blood type?\" Violet asked, her voice trembling.\n\"No, as in the kind of guy you like.\"\n\"The type who doesn't boss girls around.\"\nShocked gasps rippled through the crowd. Even the guards looked scandalized.\nAsher only smirked.\n\"How many boyfriends have you had?\"\n\"What?\"\nViolet blinked in disbelief.\nWas he looking for a mate...\nor trying to humiliate her?\nAsher tapped his foot.\n\"I'm waiting.\"\nViolet swallowed.\n\"None.\"\n\"None at all?\"\n\"Interesting.\"\nAsher's smile widened.\nViolet's stomach tightened.\nShe knew that smile.\nIt was the same cruel look she'd seen her whole life.\n\"Next question.\"\n\"Are you a virgin?\"\nViolet's face burned.\nThe whispers began immediately.\n\"Violet Purple? A virgin? Yeah, right.\"\n\"She's a whore just like her trashy mom.\"\nA lump filled Violet's throat. Hot tears burned her eyes. She'd never had a boyfriend, never even been kissed. Yet now, every district was watching people call her a whore.\n\"Answer the question, little purple,\"\nAsher taunted.\nLittle purple?\nWho does he think he is?\n\"It's none of your business,\" she snapped.\n\"Are you a virgin or not?\"\n\"I command you to answer me now.\"\nThe alpha command rippled through Violet's body. She felt a strange shudder...\n...then nothing.\nShe lifted her chin.\n\"I'm done talking.\"\nThree words.\nThat's all it took to shatter everything Asher believed.\nNo human had ever resisted a Cardinal Alpha's command.\nUntil Violet.\nAsher had no idea he'd just awakened magic hidden in her blood. All he knew was that someone had done the impossible.\nWho was this girl?\nHow had she resisted him?\nAnd why couldn't he stop looking at her?\nViolet had no idea she'd just changed everything. She thought the shaking in her hands was just nerves. She was certain she was about to be thrown to the wolves.\n\n\"Auditions are over.\"\nAsher suddenly threw up his hands.\n\"You're all dismissed.\"\nNo winner.\nNo explanation.\nThe broadcast ended as confused whispers spread through the gym.\n\"What just happened? Did she ruin it for all of us?\"\n\"Why did he stop?\"\nNone of them realized the broken girl they'd mocked minutes earlier had just done something no one else ever had.\nLater, shivering outside the school, Violet couldn't stop thinking about the strange alpha...\n...or the strange feeling he'd left beneath her skin.\nPart of her hoped she'd never see him again.\nShe had no idea he'd already decided otherwise.\nBecause once wolves start hunting...\nthey don't stop until they've caught their prey.\n\nLater that evening, Asher walked into Principal Jameson's office.\nAsher didn't need to knock.\nJameson looked up, startled.\n\"Alpha Nightshade. Visiting hours are\u2014\"\n\"The 20 girls from today's audition.\"\n\"I want their files, all of them.\"\nJameson stiffened.\n\"Those records are confidential.\"\n\"I can't just\u2014\"\nAsher's eyes locked onto hers.\n\"Bring me the files.\"\n\"Now.\"\nThe alpha command washed over Jameson.\nMoments later, the audition files sat on her desk.\n\"The girl with the purple hair.\"\nHe said,\n\"Find her.\"\nJameson's fingers stopped on one folder.\nPurple, Violet.\nAsher opened it.\n\"Read it to me.\"\nAsher ordered.\n\"Everything.\"\n\"Violet Purple, 18, District One. Single mother listed as Nancy. Prostitute. Current residence, Lot seven, Crescent Row Trailer Park, District One. Annual household income below poverty threshold. No pack affiliation. No wolf. No lineage of note.\"\nJameson stopped reading.\nAsher stared at the file.\nNo wolf.\nNo pack.\nNo one protecting her.\nYet she'd looked a Cardinal Alpha in the eye...\n...and told him no.\nHe picked up the principal's acceptance stamp.\n\"Alpha Nightshade.\"\nThe command loosened just enough for alarm to cross Jameson's face.\n\"That stamp is only for\u2014\"\nHe slammed it onto Violet's file.\nAccepted. Full Scholarship.\nJameson's eyes widened.\n\"You can't.\"\n\"I just did.\"\nAsher closed the folder.\n\"Process it tonight. Her acceptance letter arrives before morning.\"\nHe slipped his sunglasses back on.\nJameson sat frozen.\nAsher paused at the door.\n\"You will forget any of this ever happened.\"\nJameson's eyes flashed white before returning to normal.\nAsher smiled.\n\"I will see you soon, my little purple flower.\"\nHe wasn't talking to Jameson.\n\nA few days later, Violet Purple stood beneath Lunaris Academy's gothic gates.\nShe'd never applied.\nYet somehow, the academy had offered her a full scholarship.\nThe acceptance letter had simply appeared at her trailer.\nTaking a breath, she stepped through the gates.\nViolet Purple? \nA girl with sharp eyes and perfect posture approached, tablet in hand.\n\u201cI\u2019m Alice. Your student guide\u2026 and your roommate, unfortunately for both of us. You\u2019re\nthe surprise scholarship case. Lower district. No lineage. No pack affiliation. Human.\u201d\n\u201cYou forgot poor.\u201d\n\u201cThat part was obvious.\u201d\n\u201cTo compete.\u201d\n\u201cFor what?\u201d\n\u201cFor Luna.\u201d\n\u201cLike\u2026 prom queen for wolves?\u201d\nAlice didn\u2019t smile.\n\u201cThis school exists to produce one thing,\u201d \n \u201cA bond. Between a Cardinal Alpha\nand the girl most compatible with him.\u201d\n\u201cAnd how do you measure that?\u201d \n\u201cRanking.
